Data is stored and fetched only through the injected ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports; there is no storage or transport code

parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService only coordinates use cases. It loads aggregates through the ports it is given (ProductRepository, OrderRepository) and delegates the core rules to domain functions: reserve, release and dispatch (stock), and nextState and assertCancellable (order status). It also handles cross-aggregate atomicity, rolling back reservations by hand in placeOrder, and generates ids and timestamps when it creates an order. It saves results through the ports. None of this is transport work (no HTTP, request or response handling), persistence detail (no SQL, storage or serialization) or framework code. Some rules are arguably domain invariants: the quantity check, the at-least-one-line check, merging duplicate lines, and setting `order.status = "cancelled"` directly instead of through a domain transition. Moving them into the domain would be cleaner. But checking input at the use-case boundary and putting together an order across several aggregates are normal application-service work. The rubric's fail examples (persistence, transport or framework logic in the domain, or business rules in infrastructure or presentation) don't apply here.
